975.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. O my mind, repeat the Lord's Name day and night. The faults committed, many, millions upon millions: (the Name) casts them all off and puts them aside. Those who repeat and worship the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the spirit of a servant become genuine; all (their) sins and faults go out of them, as water takes away dirt. Those who sing of Nar-Narayan each moment, and with their mouths utter (the Name of) the Lord, Nar-Narhari, (from them,) from the town (of the body), (the Lord) drives out in an instant, a moment, the five untameable failings (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride). The fortunate meditate on the Lord's Name; the Lord's devotees stay green (in full bloom). O God, I beg you: grant me their company; (in it) the foolish and ignorant like me have been carried across. O Life of the world, show mercy, show mercy, and save (me), who have fallen at your refuge. Your servant Nanak is in your refuge; O Lord, keep (his) honour, O Lord. ॥4॥
Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God.
975.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Repeating (the Name of) Ram, (his) servants merge in Ram's Name itself. (They) have repeated the Name of Ram through the Guru's word, (they on whom) the merciful Lord has bestowed (his grace). The Lord, Har Har, the Master, is beyond reach and beyond the senses; (his) servants, repeating (his Name), merge (in him) as water in water. The Lord's Sants, meeting together, have found the sweet essence of Ram; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to (those) servants. The servant who has sung the Name of the Lord, the Supreme Being, has had all his poverty and pain crushed. In the body are the five untameable failings, ever restless; the Lord has destroyed them in an instant. The Lord's Sants have set their minds' love (on him), as the lotus gazes at the moon; (as,) when the cloud bends low and the dense cloud thunders, the peacock, dancing, blossoms in its mind. My Master has put a longing (for him) in me; I live by seeing the Lord and meeting (him). The Lord has given servant Nanak the craving for the Lord; O Lord, unite (me with you): (that is) true bliss. ॥4॥
975.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (your true) friend. By the Guru's grace I have meditated on the Lord's Name; I have washed the True Guru's feet. O most exalted, Lord of the world, God of the universe, keep (me), a sinner, in your refuge. You are the great Being, the destroyer of the sorrows of the lowly; O Lord, you have put (your) Name in (my) mouth. The Lord's virtues are lofty, and I am low; (yet) in the company of the Guru, the True Guru, my friend, I have sung them; as when the neem tree dwells beside the sandalwood, the qualities of the sandalwood come to dwell (in it). Our failings, born of the pleasures of Maya's poison, are many, again and again, each instant. Full of failings, heavy as stones, (we) have been carried across by the Lord in the company of (his) servants. Those whom you protect, O Lord and Master: all their sins are drawn out (of them). O merciful God, Master of servant Nanak, you have carried across even the wicked, such as Harnakhash. ॥4॥
Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu): the demon king of the Puranas who tormented his son Prahlad for his devotion to God; God, as the Man-Lion, slew him.
976.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, Ram, with love. The one on whom the Lord, Har Har, the Master of the world, has shown mercy has meditated on the Lord, falling at the feet of (his) servants. Straying and erring birth after birth, we have now come to your refuge, O God. O Master, you cherish those who come to your refuge; save us, the great sinners. In your company, O Lord, who has not been saved? O God, you have made the fallen pure. The calico printer (Namdev), singing (your) praises, was driven away as wicked; God kept the honour of (his) servant. Those who sing your praises, O Master: to them I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice. Every dwelling where the dust of (your) servants' feet has fallen, (you) have made pure. O God, we cannot tell your virtues; you are the great, great Being, the greatest of all. O God, show mercy to servant Nanak, that we may serve the feet of your servants. ॥4॥
By tradition, the priests of a temple (at Aundha) put Bhagat Namdev, a calico printer by caste, out from before it; he sat singing God's praises at the back, and the temple turned round to face him.
976.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within the mind. (The one on whom) God, the Lord of the world, has shown mercy: through the Guru's teaching (his) understanding has become (one of) the Name. The Lord's servants have sung the Lord's praise, Har Har, through the Guru's teaching, having heard the Guru; the Lord's Name has cut down (their) sins and wrongs, as a farmer reaps his fields. O God, you alone know your greatness; we cannot tell (your) virtues, O Lord. As you are, O God, so are you alone; you alone know your own virtues, O God. (Beings) are bound in the many bonds of Maya's nooses; (those who) repeated (the Name of) the Lord were set free, as the elephant held in the water by the crocodile remembered the Lord, and was released. O Master, Supreme Lord, Supreme God, (beings) have searched for you through the ages; no one has found your depth, nor can find it, O great God of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
Kunchar (Gaj): in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant (Gajendra) seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free.
976.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, in Kalyug it is the Lord's praise that is accepted. (The one on whom) God, the merciful Lord, Har Har, has shown mercy has repeated (the Name of) the Lord, falling at the True Guru's feet. O Lord, you are great, the Master beyond reach and beyond the senses; all meditate on you, the beautiful Lord. Those on whom rests your great glance (of grace) remember the Lord through the Guru. God the Master has made this (whole) expanse; the Life of the world is joined to all; as many waves of water rise in water, and water, meeting water, merges (in it). What you have done, O God, you alone know; we do not know your depth, O Lord. Set (your) praise in the hearts of us, (your) children, that we may remember God. O Lord, you are the treasure of water, the lake Mansarovar; whoever serves (you obtains) every fruit. It is the Lord, Har Har, Har Har, that servant Nanak longs for; O Lord, show mercy and grant (him this). ॥4॥
977.1: Raag Nat Narain, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mind, serve (the Lord); labour for the Lord bears fruit. Take the dust of the Guru's feet, (which) shatters all poverty and crushes pain. O mind, by the Lord's glance of grace one is filled with delight. (The body) is the Lord's home, and the Lord himself has adorned it; (it is) the palace of joys of the boundless Lord, the beloved, beloved, beloved Lord. The Lord showed his mercy and himself came into (my) home; I have made the Guru my go-between with the Lord; seeing the Lord I am delighted, delighted, delighted, delighted. The Guru brought word of the Lord's coming; on hearing that the Lord, my beloved, my beloved Lord, was coming, there was bliss upon bliss in mind and body. Servant Nanak, meeting the Lord, Har Har, is absorbed (in him); his state is delight, delight. ॥2॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
Ho ho ho: a call of address (O!) sung in the Rahao lines of these shabads; the meaning gives it as the one the shabad addresses.
977.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, join the company of the Sants, which brings forth goodness; hear (there) the telling of the One beyond telling, which brings peace; (it) takes away all sins and wrongs; O mind, (it) writes (within you) the writ of the Lord. In Kalyug the Lord's praise is the highest (deed); to dwell on (the Lord's) telling through the Guru's teaching is the (true) understanding. The one who has heard (it), the one who has believed (it): to that one I am a sacrifice. The one who has tasted the relish of the telling of the Lord beyond telling: all the hunger of that one is taken away. O Nanak, the (Lord's) servants are satisfied by hearing the Lord's telling; repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, they become (one with) the Lord. ॥2॥
977.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). If someone would come and tell (me) the talk of the Lord, of the Lord, to him I would be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice. That servant of the Lord is the best of the good. O brother, uniting (one with such a servant), the Lord fills (one) with delight. The Guru, the Sant, has told the way of the Lord; the Guru has shown how to walk, how to walk (towards) the Lord: O my Sikhs of the Guru, rid yourselves of the deceit within; without deceit, do the labour for the Lord, for the Lord, (and be) delighted, delighted, delighted. Those Sikhs of the Guru are pleasing to my Lord God who have known my Lord God to be with (them). The Lord God has given servant Nanak (this) understanding; seeing the Lord near, ever present, (he) is delighted, delighted, delighted, delighted. ॥2॥
978.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Ram, what do I know of what pleases (you)? In my mind is a great thirst for the sight of (you). He alone is wise, he alone is your servant, on whom your favour comes to rest. The one to whom you show mercy, O Being, Maker of destiny, meditates on you for ever and ever. By what yoga, what knowledge and meditation, what virtues can (anyone) win (your) pleasure? He alone is (God's) servant, he alone (God's) own devotee, on whom (God) sets the colour (of his love). That alone is understanding, that alone wisdom and skill, by which (one) does not forget God even for an instant. (The one who) has found this peace by joining the company of the Sants sings the Lord's praises for ever. (He) has seen the Wondrous One, the form of supreme joy; nothing else comes into (his) view. Says Nanak: where the Guru has removed the rust, how can the birth from the womb come there? ॥4॥
978.2: Raag Nat Narain, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I have laid blame on no one; what you do is sweet to (my) mind. Obeying (your) command and understanding (it), I have found peace; hearing your Name again and again, I live. Here and hereafter, O Lord, it is you, you alone: this teaching I have made firm (within me) from the Guru. Since I came to know this, all has been joy and well-being. Nanak has been enlightened in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy): there is no other, no second (besides God). ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
978.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) the one who has received your assurance: (his) fear of Jam (the messenger of Death) is erased, (he) has found peace, and the pain of Haumai (ego) has gone out (of him). The Amrit Bani has quenched (their) burning; (they) are satisfied as a child (is) with milk. The Sants are my mother, father and friends; the Sants are (my) helpers and brothers. (Those for whom) the doors of doubt have opened have met Gopal (the Lord who sustains all); the diamond has been pierced by the Diamond. O Nanak, singing the praise of the Master, deep in virtues, (they) are filled with wonder. ॥2॥
979.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) himself, he himself, has saved his own servant. At all hours (he) dwells with (his) servant; (he) has not let (him) slip from (his) mind. (He) did not look at all at colour or mark, nor weigh the family of (his) servant. In mercy the Lord gave (him) the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), and adorned (him) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and love. The ocean of fire is terribly hard (to cross); (God) has carried (him) across it. Beholding (God) again and again, Nanak blossoms, and again and again is a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
979.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The one who) has uttered the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within the mind: (his) millions of offences are erased in an instant, and no pain of his remains. Searching and searching, (one who) became a bairagi (one detached, longing for God) found (him) in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). Giving up all, (his) love is fixed on the One, (and he) has grasped the feet of the Lord, Har Har. Whoever has come to (God's) refuge: those who utter (the Name) are liberated, those who hear (it) are carried across. Says Nanak: remembering, remembering God, my own Master, there is bliss. ॥2॥
979.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My) cord (of love) is tied to (your) lotus feet; O Ocean of peace, bring about my supreme state. (You) have had your own servant grasp the hem (of your robe); (his) mind is pierced by the intoxication of love. Singing (your) praise, the relish of devotion has welled up (in him), and the net of Maya has been broken. The treasure of mercy is wholly pervading (all); I see no one else, no other. O Nanak, (God) has united his own servant (with himself); (his) love never grows less. ॥2॥
979.4: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my mind, repeat the chant of (the Name of) the Lord, Narayan. (O God,) may you never be forgotten by my mind, (that I may) sing (your) praises at all hours. May I bathe every day in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh, which rids (one) of all sins and wrongs. The treasure of mercy is wholly pervading (all); (he) is seen contained in every heart. Millions of chants and austerities, hundreds of thousands of worships, do not come up to the Lord's Simran (remembrance). With both palms joined, Nanak begs (this) gift: (to be) the servant of the servants of your servants. ॥2॥
979.5: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The treasure of the Naam is my all. By (God's) mercy (I) have met the company of the Saadh, and the True Guru has given (me this) gift. (God is) the Giver of peace, the Destroyer of pain; I sing (his) Kirtan (songs of God's praise), (which is) perfect knowledge. Lust, anger and greed have been broken to pieces, and foolish pride has perished. What virtues of yours can I speak of and describe, O God, Knower of hearts, all-wise? Nanak is in the refuge of (your) lotus feet, O Ocean of peace, and is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
980.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice, again and again, to the great Gopal. I am without virtue; you are the perfect Giver, Master of the lowly, merciful. Rising and sitting, sleeping and waking, (you are my) soul, breath, wealth and possessions. In my mind is a great thirst for the sight of (you); delight Nanak with the sight of (you). ॥3॥
980.2: Raag Nat Narain, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Is there any such friend, any companion of mine, who would always tell (me) the Name of the Lord, so that (my) pain and (my mind's) contrary ways would end? (To him) I would offer everything: mind, body and consciousness. Rare is the one whom (God) has made his own, whose mind is stitched to (God's) lotus feet, to whom, in mercy, (he) has given the Lord's praise. By worshipping the Lord, the priceless human birth is won; (by it) millions of the fallen become pure. Nanak, the servant, has made (himself) a sacrifice, a sacrifice (to such a one). ॥2॥
980.3: Raag Nat Narain, Ashtapadis, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Ram, in my mind and body (your) Name is (my) support. I cannot live an instant, a moment, without (your) service; through the Guru's teaching I keep the Naam in my heart. Meditate in your minds on the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har; to me the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is dear. (Those to whom) God the Master became merciful to the lowly, (he) has adorned through the Guru's Shabad. O Madhusudan, Life of the world, Madho, my Master, beyond reach and boundless, I make one prayer, one plea, before the Guru; I wash the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). God has a thousand eyes, (yet) God is the one Being, apart from all; God the Master is one, (yet has) a thousand forms; the one God carries across through the Guru's teaching. (The one who) through the Guru's teaching has found the Name of Damodar keeps the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in his heart; the telling of the Lord, Har Har, has become very sweet (to him), as a mute savours (a sweet) in gulps. The tongue tastes (other) flavours in love of duality, (but) greed and the vices are utterly tasteless; those who through the Guru taste the flavour of Ram's Name forget all other relishes and flavours. (Those who) through the Guru's teaching have found the wealth of Ram's Name have driven off (their) sins by hearing and uttering (it); Dharam Raj and Jam do not come near (them): (they) are the beloved servants of my Master. As many breaths as there are, with each breath I keep the Naam in my heart through the Guru's teaching; each breath that goes by without the Naam: that breath is wasted, in vain. Show mercy, show mercy, O God: (I am) lowly, at (your) refuge; unite me with the Lord's beloved servants. Nanak, the servant of (your) servants, says: we are the water-carriers of (your) servants. ॥8॥
Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God. Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God.
Damodar (he whose waist was bound with a cord: the child Krishna) is a name of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; in Gurbani it is a name of the one God.
981.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, we are stones, without virtue. In mercy, in mercy, (you) united (us) with the Guru, and through the Guru's Shabad carried us stones across. O True Guru, make the Name firm (within me), very sweet, the finest of all sandalwoods; through the Naam (my) awareness has spread to the ten directions, (where) the Lord gives off his fragrance like musk. Your telling, (O Lord) beyond (Maya's) qualities, is a sweet telling; the Guru has set its fine words (in the heart). (Those who) sang the Lord's praises, singing and singing: as they sang the praises, the Guru carried (them) across. The Guru is discernment, the Guru looks on all alike; casting off doubt, let us meet him. On meeting the True Guru, (I) have attained the supreme state; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru. (People) wander, practising hypocrisy upon hypocrisy; greed and hypocrisy are evils in the world. (They) bring pain here and hereafter; the messenger of Death stands over the head and strikes. When day dawns, (one) tends the snares of the household, the spread of Maya's poison; when night comes, (one) passes into dreams; even in dreams (one) tends the pains of the poison. Taking a barren field of saline earth, (he) has sown falsehood; all (his) threshing floors are of falsehood. The Saakats all stay hungry with hunger; at (their) door stand the cruel messengers of Jam. On the manmukh is a heavy debt of poison; it is cleared only by reflecting on the Shabad. All who came demanding the debts (God) has made servants (of that one), set them at (his) feet and held them back. The Lord of the world has created all beings; all are held by the cord through the nose. O Nanak, as God pulls, as pleases the beloved Ram, so one has to walk. ॥8॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
981.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, (the Guru) has bathed (me) in the pool of the Lord's Amrit. The knowledge the True Guru gives is the finest bath; meeting (him), the filth of sins is washed away. The virtue of good company is very great: the parrot, by learning to say (Ram's Name), carried Ganika across. (Krishna's) touch came to Kubija, whom none would touch, and took her to Baikunth (heaven). Ajamal loved (his) son, and called (him) by the name Narayan; (that) feeling of love pleased my Master's mind, (and he) struck down and drove off the messengers of Death. A man talks (wisdom), and talking, makes people hear it, (but) does not reflect on what he says. If he finds the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), firmness comes (to him), (and) through the Name of the Lord, Ram, he is carried across. As long as soul and body are whole, so long (he) keeps nothing (of God) in mind; when the house and mansion have caught fire, (then) he digs a well and draws water from it. O mind, do not keep company with the Saakat, who has let the Name of the Lord, Har Har, slip from his mind. The Saakat's words sting like a scorpion; leave the Saakat, (and stay) far, far away. (Those who), clinging again and again, have formed great love (for God) are adorned by clinging to the company of the Saadh; (those who) have accepted the Guru's words as true, as true, are very dear to my Master. (Those who) earned (good deeds) little by little in a former birth have come to hold the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har, dear; (such a one) has found, by the Guru's grace, the relish of Amrit; (he) sings of that relish, reflects on that relish. O Lord, Har Har, all forms and colours are yours, O my Beloved, my deep-red Darling. As the colour you give, so does (a being) become; what can poor creatures (do), O Nanak? ॥8॥

Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram; Kubija: the hunchbacked maid of Kans, made straight and fair by Krishna; Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called his son Narayan.
982.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, in the Guru's refuge, God is the protector, as when the crocodile seized the elephant and dragged it off, (and God) lifted it up, drew it out and saved it. God's servants are very, very good; with faith in their minds, (they) enshrine the Lord. Faith and devotion please the mind of my God, (and he) upholds the honour of his servant. The servant of the Lord, Har Har, who is engaged in (his) service sees all as the expanse of Brahm (God); (to him) the one Being, the One alone, comes into view, (who) looks upon all with a single glance. The Lord God, the Master, pervades all places, (and) cares for the whole world as (his) handmaid. (He,) the Merciful, himself gives the gift of mercy; (he) has made (even) the worms within the stones. Within (the deer) is the strong scent of musk, (yet) the deer, misled by doubt, butts at (the bushes) with its horns; (the soul-bride) has grown weary, searching and searching from forest to forest; the perfect Guru has saved (her) in (her own) home. The Bani is the Guru, and the Guru is the Bani; within the Bani is all Amrit. The Guru speaks the Bani, (and) the servant who believes (it) the Guru carries across, before (all) eyes. All is Brahm, Brahm is spread out (everywhere); (yet each) eats what (he) has sown in the mind, as Dhrishtabuddhi, who tormented the devotee Chandrahans, set fire to his own house with a firebrand. The servant longs for God within the heart; God keeps watch over the servant's breaths. In mercy, in mercy, (God) makes devotion firm (in him), and carries across the world that follows (his) servant. God the Master is himself, all by himself; God himself adorns the creation. O servant Nanak, (God) himself, he himself, pervades all; in mercy he himself carries (beings) across. ॥8॥
Chandrahans: a king's son and a devotee of God, whom the minister Dhrishtabuddhi tried to have killed; by mistake it was Dhrishtabuddhi's own son who was killed.
982.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Ram, show mercy and save (me), as when the wicked seized Dropati and brought her (into the court), and the Lord, Har Har, saved her from shame. Show mercy, O Beloved; (we are) your servants, beggars; I beg (you) for one gift: a longing for the True Guru is ever with me; O Lord, unite me with the Guru and adorn (me). The Saakat's deeds are like churning water; (he) churns and churns water for ever. (The one who), joining the Sat Sangat, has attained the supreme state draws out the butter and swallows it with relish. (One who) bathed the body day after day, rubbed and rubbed and adorned the body every day, (but whose) mind was not pleased by my True Guru's words: all (his) fine adornments are hollow. Walk with a joyful sway, O companion, my friend, keeping my Master's virtues in your heart. Service through the Guru pleases my God; O True Guru, make me perceive the Imperceptible. Woman or man, man or all women: all is the one Being, Murari (the foe of the demon Mur). The dust of the Sants' feet has pleased (my) mind; meeting the Lord's servants, (one is) carried across by the Lord. I wandered through village after village and all the towns; the Lord's servants have found (him) within the heart. Bringing forth faith, faith (in me), (God) has united (me with the Guru); the Lord has carried me across through the Guru, the Guru. The True Guru has made the whole thread of (my) breaths good; (I) reflect on the Shabad. Going into (my) own home, (I) have drunk the relish of Amrit; (I) behold the world without (these) eyes. O Lord, I cannot describe your virtues; you are the temple, we are tiny worms (in it). Says Nanak: show mercy, unite (me with) the Guru, (that) my mind may be steadied, repeating Ram. ॥8॥
Dropati (Draupadi): in the Mahabharata, the wife of the Pandavas, dragged by the Kauravas before the full court to be stripped; she called on Krishna, and her cloth never came to an end.
983.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, worship the Master, beyond reach and boundless. We are sinners, utterly without virtue; in mercy, the Guru has carried (us) across. (I) have found the holy Being, the holy servant (the Guru); I make one plea to the beloved Guru: give (me) the wealth of Ram's Name as (my) capital, (which) takes away all thirst and hunger. The moth burns away; the deer, the bumblebee, the elephant and the fish are each seized by one sense and destroyed; in the body are the five mighty demons (lust and the other vices); the Guru, the True Guru, drives out the sins. (I) have searched and searched the Shastras and the Vedas; the sage Narad too proclaimed (this) word: repeat the Name of Ram, and you will be set free; in the Sat Sangat the Guru has carried (beings) across. Love for the Beloved, God, has taken hold, as the lotus gazes at the sun; (as) the peacock dances on the high mountains when the dense clouds bend low. Water the Saakat with much Amrit: all (his) branches and flowers (stay) poisonous. The more one bows before a Saakat man, the more he stirs up trouble and spits out bitter poison. Let us live joined with the Sants, the Sant folk and the holy; they speak of (God's) virtues and do good to others. When a Sant meets a Sant, the mind blossoms, as lotuses, meeting water, are made beautiful. The wave of greed is wholly a mad dog; the mad (dog) corrupts all. Word reached my Master's court, (and) the Guru took up the sword of knowledge and killed (it). Save (me), save (me), save (me), O my God; show mercy and save me. Says Nanak: I have no other support; the True Guru, the Guru, has carried me across.

Each of these creatures dies through one sense: the bumble-bee through smell, shut in the closing lotus; the moth through sight, in the flame; the elephant through touch, lured into a pit by a she-elephant; the fish through taste, on the bait; the deer through hearing, drawn by the hunter's music.
Narad is a sage of the Puranas, messenger of the gods and a devotee of Vishnu.
Chhaka 1: the first set of six shabads; the count is written after the shabad's numbers.

975.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
O my mind, repeat the Lord's Name day and night.
The faults committed, many, millions upon millions: (the Name) casts them all off and puts them aside.
Those who repeat and worship the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the spirit of a servant become genuine;
all (their) sins and faults go out of them, as water takes away dirt.
Those who sing of Nar-Narayan each moment, and with their mouths utter (the Name of) the Lord, Nar-Narhari,
(from them,) from the town (of the body), (the Lord) drives out in an instant, a moment, the five untameable failings (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride).
The fortunate meditate on the Lord's Name; the Lord's devotees stay green (in full bloom).
O God, I beg you: grant me their company; (in it) the foolish and ignorant like me have been carried across.
O Life of the world, show mercy, show mercy, and save (me), who have fallen at your refuge.
Your servant Nanak is in your refuge; O Lord, keep (his) honour, O Lord. ॥4॥
975.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Repeating (the Name of) Ram, (his) servants merge in Ram's Name itself.
(They) have repeated the Name of Ram through the Guru's word, (they on whom) the merciful Lord has bestowed (his grace).
The Lord, Har Har, the Master, is beyond reach and beyond the senses; (his) servants, repeating (his Name), merge (in him) as water in water.
The Lord's Sants, meeting together, have found the sweet essence of Ram; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to (those) servants.
The servant who has sung the Name of the Lord, the Supreme Being, has had all his poverty and pain crushed.
In the body are the five untameable failings, ever restless; the Lord has destroyed them in an instant.
The Lord's Sants have set their minds' love (on him), as the lotus gazes at the moon;
(as,) when the cloud bends low and the dense cloud thunders, the peacock, dancing, blossoms in its mind.
My Master has put a longing (for him) in me; I live by seeing the Lord and meeting (him).
The Lord has given servant Nanak the craving for the Lord; O Lord, unite (me with you): (that is) true bliss. ॥4॥
975.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (your true) friend.
By the Guru's grace I have meditated on the Lord's Name; I have washed the True Guru's feet.
O most exalted, Lord of the world, God of the universe, keep (me), a sinner, in your refuge.
You are the great Being, the destroyer of the sorrows of the lowly; O Lord, you have put (your) Name in (my) mouth.
The Lord's virtues are lofty, and I am low; (yet) in the company of the Guru, the True Guru, my friend, I have sung them;
as when the neem tree dwells beside the sandalwood, the qualities of the sandalwood come to dwell (in it).
Our failings, born of the pleasures of Maya's poison, are many, again and again, each instant.
Full of failings, heavy as stones, (we) have been carried across by the Lord in the company of (his) servants.
Those whom you protect, O Lord and Master: all their sins are drawn out (of them).
O merciful God, Master of servant Nanak, you have carried across even the wicked, such as Harnakhash. ॥4॥
976.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, Ram, with love.
The one on whom the Lord, Har Har, the Master of the world, has shown mercy has meditated on the Lord, falling at the feet of (his) servants.
Straying and erring birth after birth, we have now come to your refuge, O God.
O Master, you cherish those who come to your refuge; save us, the great sinners.
In your company, O Lord, who has not been saved? O God, you have made the fallen pure.
The calico printer (Namdev), singing (your) praises, was driven away as wicked; God kept the honour of (his) servant.
Those who sing your praises, O Master: to them I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice.
Every dwelling where the dust of (your) servants' feet has fallen, (you) have made pure.
O God, we cannot tell your virtues; you are the great, great Being, the greatest of all.
O God, show mercy to servant Nanak, that we may serve the feet of your servants. ॥4॥
976.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within the mind.
(The one on whom) God, the Lord of the world, has shown mercy: through the Guru's teaching (his) understanding has become (one of) the Name.
The Lord's servants have sung the Lord's praise, Har Har, through the Guru's teaching, having heard the Guru;
the Lord's Name has cut down (their) sins and wrongs, as a farmer reaps his fields.
O God, you alone know your greatness; we cannot tell (your) virtues, O Lord.
As you are, O God, so are you alone; you alone know your own virtues, O God.
(Beings) are bound in the many bonds of Maya's nooses; (those who) repeated (the Name of) the Lord were set free,
as the elephant held in the water by the crocodile remembered the Lord, and was released.
O Master, Supreme Lord, Supreme God, (beings) have searched for you through the ages;
no one has found your depth, nor can find it, O great God of servant Nanak. ॥4॥
976.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, in Kalyug it is the Lord's praise that is accepted.
(The one on whom) God, the merciful Lord, Har Har, has shown mercy has repeated (the Name of) the Lord, falling at the True Guru's feet.
O Lord, you are great, the Master beyond reach and beyond the senses; all meditate on you, the beautiful Lord.
Those on whom rests your great glance (of grace) remember the Lord through the Guru.
God the Master has made this (whole) expanse; the Life of the world is joined to all;
as many waves of water rise in water, and water, meeting water, merges (in it).
What you have done, O God, you alone know; we do not know your depth, O Lord.
Set (your) praise in the hearts of us, (your) children, that we may remember God.
O Lord, you are the treasure of water, the lake Mansarovar; whoever serves (you obtains) every fruit.
It is the Lord, Har Har, Har Har, that servant Nanak longs for; O Lord, show mercy and grant (him this). ॥4॥
977.1: Raag Nat Narain, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O my mind, serve (the Lord); labour for the Lord bears fruit.
Take the dust of the Guru's feet,
(which) shatters all poverty and crushes pain.
O mind, by the Lord's glance of grace one is filled with delight.
(The body) is the Lord's home, and the Lord himself has adorned it; (it is) the palace of joys of the boundless Lord, the beloved, beloved, beloved Lord.
The Lord showed his mercy and himself came into (my) home; I have made the Guru my go-between with the Lord; seeing the Lord I am delighted, delighted, delighted, delighted.
The Guru brought word of the Lord's coming; on hearing that the Lord, my beloved, my beloved Lord, was coming, there was bliss upon bliss in mind and body.
Servant Nanak, meeting the Lord, Har Har, is absorbed (in him); his state is delight, delight. ॥2॥
977.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O mind, join the company of the Sants, which brings forth goodness;
hear (there) the telling of the One beyond telling, which brings peace;
(it) takes away all sins and wrongs;
O mind, (it) writes (within you) the writ of the Lord.
In Kalyug the Lord's praise is the highest (deed); to dwell on (the Lord's) telling through the Guru's teaching is the (true) understanding.
The one who has heard (it), the one who has believed (it): to that one I am a sacrifice.
The one who has tasted the relish of the telling of the Lord beyond telling: all the hunger of that one is taken away.
O Nanak, the (Lord's) servants are satisfied by hearing the Lord's telling; repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, they become (one with) the Lord. ॥2॥
977.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If someone would come and tell (me) the talk of the Lord, of the Lord,
to him I would be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice.
That servant of the Lord is the best of the good.
O brother, uniting (one with such a servant), the Lord fills (one) with delight.
The Guru, the Sant, has told the way of the Lord; the Guru has shown how to walk, how to walk (towards) the Lord:
O my Sikhs of the Guru, rid yourselves of the deceit within; without deceit, do the labour for the Lord, for the Lord, (and be) delighted, delighted, delighted.
Those Sikhs of the Guru are pleasing to my Lord God who have known my Lord God to be with (them).
The Lord God has given servant Nanak (this) understanding; seeing the Lord near, ever present, (he) is delighted, delighted, delighted, delighted. ॥2॥
978.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Ram, what do I know of what pleases (you)?
In my mind is a great thirst for the sight of (you).
He alone is wise, he alone is your servant, on whom your favour comes to rest.
The one to whom you show mercy, O Being, Maker of destiny, meditates on you for ever and ever.
By what yoga, what knowledge and meditation, what virtues can (anyone) win (your) pleasure?
He alone is (God's) servant, he alone (God's) own devotee, on whom (God) sets the colour (of his love).
That alone is understanding, that alone wisdom and skill, by which (one) does not forget God even for an instant.
(The one who) has found this peace by joining the company of the Sants sings the Lord's praises for ever.
(He) has seen the Wondrous One, the form of supreme joy; nothing else comes into (his) view.
Says Nanak: where the Guru has removed the rust, how can the birth from the womb come there? ॥4॥
978.2: Raag Nat Narain, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have laid blame on no one;
what you do is sweet to (my) mind.
Obeying (your) command and understanding (it), I have found peace; hearing your Name again and again, I live.
Here and hereafter, O Lord, it is you, you alone: this teaching I have made firm (within me) from the Guru.
Since I came to know this, all has been joy and well-being.
Nanak has been enlightened in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy): there is no other, no second (besides God). ॥2॥
978.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) the one who has received your assurance:
(his) fear of Jam (the messenger of Death) is erased, (he) has found peace, and the pain of Haumai (ego) has gone out (of him).
The Amrit Bani has quenched (their) burning; (they) are satisfied as a child (is) with milk.
The Sants are my mother, father and friends; the Sants are (my) helpers and brothers.
(Those for whom) the doors of doubt have opened have met Gopal (the Lord who sustains all); the diamond has been pierced by the Diamond.
O Nanak, singing the praise of the Master, deep in virtues, (they) are filled with wonder. ॥2॥
979.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) himself, he himself, has saved his own servant.
At all hours (he) dwells with (his) servant; (he) has not let (him) slip from (his) mind.
(He) did not look at all at colour or mark, nor weigh the family of (his) servant.
In mercy the Lord gave (him) the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), and adorned (him) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and love.
The ocean of fire is terribly hard (to cross); (God) has carried (him) across it.
Beholding (God) again and again, Nanak blossoms, and again and again is a sacrifice (to him). ॥2॥
979.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The one who) has uttered the Name of the Lord, Har Har, within the mind:
(his) millions of offences are erased in an instant, and no pain of his remains.
Searching and searching, (one who) became a bairagi (one detached, longing for God) found (him) in the company of the Saadh (the Guru).
Giving up all, (his) love is fixed on the One, (and he) has grasped the feet of the Lord, Har Har.
Whoever has come to (God's) refuge: those who utter (the Name) are liberated, those who hear (it) are carried across.
Says Nanak: remembering, remembering God, my own Master, there is bliss. ॥2॥
979.3: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My) cord (of love) is tied to (your) lotus feet;
O Ocean of peace, bring about my supreme state.
(You) have had your own servant grasp the hem (of your robe); (his) mind is pierced by the intoxication of love.
Singing (your) praise, the relish of devotion has welled up (in him), and the net of Maya has been broken.
The treasure of mercy is wholly pervading (all); I see no one else, no other.
O Nanak, (God) has united his own servant (with himself); (his) love never grows less. ॥2॥
979.4: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, repeat the chant of (the Name of) the Lord, Narayan.
(O God,) may you never be forgotten by my mind, (that I may) sing (your) praises at all hours.
May I bathe every day in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh, which rids (one) of all sins and wrongs.
The treasure of mercy is wholly pervading (all); (he) is seen contained in every heart.
Millions of chants and austerities, hundreds of thousands of worships, do not come up to the Lord's Simran (remembrance).
With both palms joined, Nanak begs (this) gift: (to be) the servant of the servants of your servants. ॥2॥
979.5: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The treasure of the Naam is my all.
By (God's) mercy (I) have met the company of the Saadh, and the True Guru has given (me this) gift.
(God is) the Giver of peace, the Destroyer of pain; I sing (his) Kirtan (songs of God's praise), (which is) perfect knowledge.
Lust, anger and greed have been broken to pieces, and foolish pride has perished.
What virtues of yours can I speak of and describe, O God, Knower of hearts, all-wise?
Nanak is in the refuge of (your) lotus feet, O Ocean of peace, and is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
980.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice, again and again, to the great Gopal.
I am without virtue; you are the perfect Giver, Master of the lowly, merciful.
Rising and sitting, sleeping and waking, (you are my) soul, breath, wealth and possessions.
In my mind is a great thirst for the sight of (you); delight Nanak with the sight of (you). ॥3॥
980.2: Raag Nat Narain, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Is there any such friend, any companion of mine,
who would always tell (me) the Name of the Lord,
so that (my) pain and (my mind's) contrary ways would end?
(To him) I would offer everything: mind, body and consciousness.
Rare is the one whom (God) has made his own,
whose mind is stitched to (God's) lotus feet,
to whom, in mercy, (he) has given the Lord's praise.
By worshipping the Lord, the priceless human birth is won;
(by it) millions of the fallen become pure.
Nanak, the servant, has made (himself) a sacrifice, a sacrifice (to such a one). ॥2॥
980.3: Raag Nat Narain, Ashtapadis, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Ram, in my mind and body (your) Name is (my) support.
I cannot live an instant, a moment, without (your) service; through the Guru's teaching I keep the Naam in my heart.
Meditate in your minds on the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har; to me the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is dear.
(Those to whom) God the Master became merciful to the lowly, (he) has adorned through the Guru's Shabad.
O Madhusudan, Life of the world, Madho, my Master, beyond reach and boundless,
I make one prayer, one plea, before the Guru; I wash the feet of the Saadh (the Guru).
God has a thousand eyes, (yet) God is the one Being, apart from all;
God the Master is one, (yet has) a thousand forms; the one God carries across through the Guru's teaching.
(The one who) through the Guru's teaching has found the Name of Damodar keeps the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in his heart;
the telling of the Lord, Har Har, has become very sweet (to him), as a mute savours (a sweet) in gulps.
The tongue tastes (other) flavours in love of duality, (but) greed and the vices are utterly tasteless;
those who through the Guru taste the flavour of Ram's Name forget all other relishes and flavours.
(Those who) through the Guru's teaching have found the wealth of Ram's Name have driven off (their) sins by hearing and uttering (it);
Dharam Raj and Jam do not come near (them): (they) are the beloved servants of my Master.
As many breaths as there are, with each breath I keep the Naam in my heart through the Guru's teaching;
each breath that goes by without the Naam: that breath is wasted, in vain.
Show mercy, show mercy, O God: (I am) lowly, at (your) refuge; unite me with the Lord's beloved servants.
Nanak, the servant of (your) servants, says: we are the water-carriers of (your) servants. ॥8॥
981.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, we are stones, without virtue.
In mercy, in mercy, (you) united (us) with the Guru, and through the Guru's Shabad carried us stones across.
O True Guru, make the Name firm (within me), very sweet, the finest of all sandalwoods;
through the Naam (my) awareness has spread to the ten directions, (where) the Lord gives off his fragrance like musk.
Your telling, (O Lord) beyond (Maya's) qualities, is a sweet telling; the Guru has set its fine words (in the heart).
(Those who) sang the Lord's praises, singing and singing: as they sang the praises, the Guru carried (them) across.
The Guru is discernment, the Guru looks on all alike; casting off doubt, let us meet him.
On meeting the True Guru, (I) have attained the supreme state; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru.
(People) wander, practising hypocrisy upon hypocrisy; greed and hypocrisy are evils in the world.
(They) bring pain here and hereafter; the messenger of Death stands over the head and strikes.
When day dawns, (one) tends the snares of the household, the spread of Maya's poison;
when night comes, (one) passes into dreams; even in dreams (one) tends the pains of the poison.
Taking a barren field of saline earth, (he) has sown falsehood; all (his) threshing floors are of falsehood.
The Saakats all stay hungry with hunger; at (their) door stand the cruel messengers of Jam.
On the manmukh is a heavy debt of poison; it is cleared only by reflecting on the Shabad.
All who came demanding the debts (God) has made servants (of that one), set them at (his) feet and held them back.
The Lord of the world has created all beings; all are held by the cord through the nose.
O Nanak, as God pulls, as pleases the beloved Ram, so one has to walk. ॥8॥
981.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, (the Guru) has bathed (me) in the pool of the Lord's Amrit.
The knowledge the True Guru gives is the finest bath; meeting (him), the filth of sins is washed away.
The virtue of good company is very great: the parrot, by learning to say (Ram's Name), carried Ganika across.
(Krishna's) touch came to Kubija, whom none would touch, and took her to Baikunth (heaven).
Ajamal loved (his) son, and called (him) by the name Narayan;
(that) feeling of love pleased my Master's mind, (and he) struck down and drove off the messengers of Death.
A man talks (wisdom), and talking, makes people hear it, (but) does not reflect on what he says.
If he finds the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), firmness comes (to him), (and) through the Name of the Lord, Ram, he is carried across.
As long as soul and body are whole, so long (he) keeps nothing (of God) in mind;
when the house and mansion have caught fire, (then) he digs a well and draws water from it.
O mind, do not keep company with the Saakat, who has let the Name of the Lord, Har Har, slip from his mind.
The Saakat's words sting like a scorpion; leave the Saakat, (and stay) far, far away.
(Those who), clinging again and again, have formed great love (for God) are adorned by clinging to the company of the Saadh;
(those who) have accepted the Guru's words as true, as true, are very dear to my Master.
(Those who) earned (good deeds) little by little in a former birth have come to hold the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har, dear;
(such a one) has found, by the Guru's grace, the relish of Amrit; (he) sings of that relish, reflects on that relish.
O Lord, Har Har, all forms and colours are yours, O my Beloved, my deep-red Darling.
As the colour you give, so does (a being) become; what can poor creatures (do), O Nanak? ॥8॥
982.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, in the Guru's refuge, God is the protector,
as when the crocodile seized the elephant and dragged it off, (and God) lifted it up, drew it out and saved it.
God's servants are very, very good; with faith in their minds, (they) enshrine the Lord.
Faith and devotion please the mind of my God, (and he) upholds the honour of his servant.
The servant of the Lord, Har Har, who is engaged in (his) service sees all as the expanse of Brahm (God);
(to him) the one Being, the One alone, comes into view, (who) looks upon all with a single glance.
The Lord God, the Master, pervades all places, (and) cares for the whole world as (his) handmaid.
(He,) the Merciful, himself gives the gift of mercy; (he) has made (even) the worms within the stones.
Within (the deer) is the strong scent of musk, (yet) the deer, misled by doubt, butts at (the bushes) with its horns;
(the soul-bride) has grown weary, searching and searching from forest to forest; the perfect Guru has saved (her) in (her own) home.
The Bani is the Guru, and the Guru is the Bani; within the Bani is all Amrit.
The Guru speaks the Bani, (and) the servant who believes (it) the Guru carries across, before (all) eyes.
All is Brahm, Brahm is spread out (everywhere); (yet each) eats what (he) has sown in the mind,
as Dhrishtabuddhi, who tormented the devotee Chandrahans, set fire to his own house with a firebrand.
The servant longs for God within the heart; God keeps watch over the servant's breaths.
In mercy, in mercy, (God) makes devotion firm (in him), and carries across the world that follows (his) servant.
God the Master is himself, all by himself; God himself adorns the creation.
O servant Nanak, (God) himself, he himself, pervades all; in mercy he himself carries (beings) across. ॥8॥
982.2: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Ram, show mercy and save (me),
as when the wicked seized Dropati and brought her (into the court), and the Lord, Har Har, saved her from shame.
Show mercy, O Beloved; (we are) your servants, beggars; I beg (you) for one gift:
a longing for the True Guru is ever with me; O Lord, unite me with the Guru and adorn (me).
The Saakat's deeds are like churning water; (he) churns and churns water for ever.
(The one who), joining the Sat Sangat, has attained the supreme state draws out the butter and swallows it with relish.
(One who) bathed the body day after day, rubbed and rubbed and adorned the body every day,
(but whose) mind was not pleased by my True Guru's words: all (his) fine adornments are hollow.
Walk with a joyful sway, O companion, my friend, keeping my Master's virtues in your heart.
Service through the Guru pleases my God; O True Guru, make me perceive the Imperceptible.
Woman or man, man or all women: all is the one Being, Murari (the foe of the demon Mur).
The dust of the Sants' feet has pleased (my) mind; meeting the Lord's servants, (one is) carried across by the Lord.
I wandered through village after village and all the towns; the Lord's servants have found (him) within the heart.
Bringing forth faith, faith (in me), (God) has united (me with the Guru); the Lord has carried me across through the Guru, the Guru.
The True Guru has made the whole thread of (my) breaths good; (I) reflect on the Shabad.
Going into (my) own home, (I) have drunk the relish of Amrit; (I) behold the world without (these) eyes.
O Lord, I cannot describe your virtues; you are the temple, we are tiny worms (in it).
Says Nanak: show mercy, unite (me with) the Guru, (that) my mind may be steadied, repeating Ram. ॥8॥
983.1: Raag Nat Narain, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my mind, worship the Master, beyond reach and boundless.
We are sinners, utterly without virtue; in mercy, the Guru has carried (us) across.
(I) have found the holy Being, the holy servant (the Guru); I make one plea to the beloved Guru:
give (me) the wealth of Ram's Name as (my) capital, (which) takes away all thirst and hunger.
The moth burns away; the deer, the bumblebee, the elephant and the fish are each seized by one sense and destroyed;
in the body are the five mighty demons (lust and the other vices); the Guru, the True Guru, drives out the sins.
(I) have searched and searched the Shastras and the Vedas; the sage Narad too proclaimed (this) word:
repeat the Name of Ram, and you will be set free; in the Sat Sangat the Guru has carried (beings) across.
Love for the Beloved, God, has taken hold, as the lotus gazes at the sun;
(as) the peacock dances on the high mountains when the dense clouds bend low.
Water the Saakat with much Amrit: all (his) branches and flowers (stay) poisonous.
The more one bows before a Saakat man, the more he stirs up trouble and spits out bitter poison.
Let us live joined with the Sants, the Sant folk and the holy; they speak of (God's) virtues and do good to others.
When a Sant meets a Sant, the mind blossoms, as lotuses, meeting water, are made beautiful.
The wave of greed is wholly a mad dog; the mad (dog) corrupts all.
Word reached my Master's court, (and) the Guru took up the sword of knowledge and killed (it).
Save (me), save (me), save (me), O my God; show mercy and save me.
Says Nanak: I have no other support; the True Guru, the Guru, has carried me across.
